name: VaultSparkStudios.github.io
currentFocus: Session 338 ran the arc under founder authorization for a direct push to main and a full production deploy, and its three findings were all gates that were not doing what their names promised. FIRST: the red uptime-probe cron was not the ordering race the board recorded. Reproduced locally, build-deploy-currency drifted between --probe and --check because observationFromReceipt() never restored the three content-clock fields added in S336 — the third time a field was added to the emitter and forgotten in the reader (after retainedForHours in S300 and historyComplete in S316). The consequence was far larger than a red cron: classify() reads contentLagHours, so every non-probe re-derive — npm run build:check, the content lane, every local build — collapsed it to null, which silently disabled the content ceiling S336 built specifically to catch a whole release stranded in production. Fixed, and the class closed with a fixed-point self-test that names no field (derive(read(derive(x))) === derive(x)) plus a companion case proving that guard can fail; 87/87, was 85. Notably an S300 test of exactly this shape already existed and stayed green throughout, because its fixtures omitted the dropped fields. SECOND: Lighthouse CI had been red for 15 consecutive runs across ~27 hours, so the site's performance gate had produced no verdict for over a day and nothing said so. /ranks/ was consolidated into /leaderboards/#ranks and answered by a _redirects 301, but three CI audit-target lists still named it — including the one auditing the LOCAL PREVIEW, which serves the built tree with no edge layer, so the redirect cannot apply and Lighthouse 404'd on a page that cannot exist there. /vaultsparked/ was in the same state. Both removed, and scripts/check-workflow-audit-targets.mjs added to build:check with two rules that name no route: no target may be a `from` in route-consolidation.json, and every local-preview target must resolve to a real page. THIRD: staging parity was a hand-maintained three-route sample and structurally could not see an absent route, which is why S337 could only record /how-we-build/ as an anecdote. It now compares the surface each origin advertises: production advertises 134 routes, staging 115, 23 missing on staging including /evidence/, /how-we-build/, three news editions and the whole .ai/ layer, with staging's build-sha reporting 94e78e93 built 2026-08-28 — five days behind production. Published as surfaceParity with gating:false and the reason stated on the artifact, because gating on a known-open blocker is a self-inflicted release outage. OUTCOME: closed out, pushed directly to main, and fully deployed to production. FOURTH, surfaced by converging the gate rather than by the audit: build-news-visual-receipts hashes each story's rendered page but ran four steps before build-shell-assets rewrote them, so it was stale by construction on every shell rotation and its own error message prescribed a hand-rebuild rather than the ordering fix; moved after every page rewriter and immediately before the seal, which also removes a confound from the standing build-to-build churn investigation. The visual and mobile proof receipts were then recaptured against the final tree: no UI changed, so CANON-053 was not triggered, but those receipts bind the candidate manifest sha rather than any appearance, and every reseal invalidates them.
publicNote: Three of the site's own safety checks were quietly not working. One had switched off an alarm meant to catch a release that never reaches readers; one had left the site's speed check failing for over a day without saying so; and one could not notice when the test environment falls behind the live site — it now measures exactly how far, and it is five days and 23 pages behind. All three are fixed or measured, and everything here is live: the site was fully redeployed and verified.
nextMilestone: Find and fix whatever refreshes the staging origin — it stopped on 2026-08-28 and is 23 advertised routes behind production — then flip surfaceParity to gating so CANON-007 stops running backwards. Then hoist the Trusted Types default-policy installer ahead of the 31 client assets that load before it and decide the founder-approved enforce flip on fresh evidence, the founder privacy decision on the four silent-zero tables, and the manual CANON-053 rendered-pixel review of the newly-served surfaces.
blockers: TRUSTED TYPES ENFORCE: blocked by a named defect, not only by stale evidence. ambient-core.bundle.js installs the TT default policy that the site's ~167 legacy innerHTML sinks depend on, and its own comment says it MUST load before any sink usage — but it is not the first script on the page. Measured across 137 built pages in S337: 31 sink-bearing assets load before it (pwa-nav.js 81 pages, pwa-install.js 72). Report-Only hides this; enforcement throws. The repair rewrites every page head and invalidates every hash-bound receipt, so it is a session of its own (D-S337.3).

identity/auth surfaces remain held on real-provider-e2e-pending (obelisk.identity.verify missing OBELISK_RP_ID/RP_NAME/RP_ORIGIN; obelisk-staging-registration missing). NOTE (S337, D-S337.1): this holds the IDENTITY BLAST RADIUS only — auth/**, surface:identity, worker:identity. It does NOT block a full production deploy: the S319 scoped path returns allowed=true mode=scoped for any candidate disjoint from that radius, and did so this session.

STAGING IS FIVE DAYS BEHIND PRODUCTION, now measured rather than anecdotal (S338, D-S338.3). check-staging-parity compares advertised sitemaps: production 134 routes, staging 115, 23 missing — /evidence/, /how-we-build/, three news editions and the whole .ai/ fact-sheet layer — and staging's api/build-sha.json reports 94e78e93 built 2026-08-28. CANON-007 makes staging the thing production is verified against, so the release ceremony's browser matrix is clearing a tree five days newer than the one it measures. surfaceParity is published with gating:false on purpose: gating on a known-open blocker would be a self-inflicted release outage. Unblock by establishing what deploys the Hetzner staging origin and why it stopped, then flip gating.

PRIVACY DECISION (founder): four public tables — challenge_submissions, game_sessions, point_events, member_achievements — have no anonymous read path, so /community/, all seven /leaderboards/* and public member profiles render zeros and empty states to signed-out visitors. The fix generalizes the S335 public_leaderboard pattern, but it decides which member activity becomes publicly readable and is escalated rather than applied (D-S336.5).

identity: the provider chain is live and verified; production promotion is held only on the real-provider journey, whose remaining leg is a founder passkey ceremony — hardware-key enrollment is founder-reserved by CANON-019 and is deliberately not automatable.

Trusted Types enforcement stays held. Founder approved the flip in S335, but api/tt-readiness.json now honestly reports stale-evidence: its soak manifest is 57 days old against a declared 30-day window. The ageing defect is fixed; the missing input is a fresh KV soak, not a code change.
rollback architecture: the GitHub Pages warm origin still follows mutable main; D-S303 requires explicit founder authorization before migrating to an immutable verified generation.
IGNIS freshness: stale in a studio-ops portfolio artifact this repo cannot write; resolve upstream rather than backdating.
The Dispatch has zero confirmed subscribers until the founder clicks the double-opt-in confirmation email.

startup-revenue-agreement is red: the promoted v5 startup brief renders a revenue evidence age the shared resolver disagrees with, and context/SIGNALS.md is stale. Studio-ops brief-renderer owned; must not be fixed by editing the sibling repo.
